subsystems.name: Qubit register
subsystems.role: stores the quantum state of the number being factored and the work register.

subsystems.name: Quantum gate control
subsystems.role: applies the precise sequence of quantum gates that perform the arithmetic.

subsystems.name: Error-correction layer
subsystems.role: encodes each logical qubit into many physical qubits and corrects errors in real time.

subsystems.name: Modular exponentiation circuit
subsystems.role: computes a^x mod N in superposition, the core arithmetic of the algorithm.

subsystems.name: Quantum Fourier transform
subsystems.role: converts the period of the function into measurable probabilities.

subsystems.name: Classical pre- and post-processing
subsystems.role: chooses the base a, and extracts factors from the measured output using continued fractions.

buildSteps.title: Build a small qubit processor
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate a handful of physical qubits with basic gates and readout, enough to run simple circuits.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate the arithmetic
buildSteps.detail: Implement and test quantum adders and modular multipliers on small numbers, verifying against classical results.

buildSteps.title: Run Shor's algorithm on small composites
buildSteps.detail: Use the machine to factor numbers such as 15 or 21, checking that the measured period yields the correct factors.

buildSteps.title: Add error correction
buildSteps.detail: Encode one logical qubit into many physical qubits, show that it lives longer and computes more accurately than any single physical qubit.

buildSteps.title: Scale logical qubits
buildSteps.detail: Increase the number of logical qubits and gate fidelity until the circuit for a chosen number fits and runs reliably.

buildSteps.title: Integrate real-time control
buildSteps.detail: Build classical electronics and software that measure error syndromes and feed back corrections within the qubit coherence time.

buildSteps.title: Target a cryptographic size
buildSteps.detail: Repeat for a number used in public-key cryptography, such as a 2048-bit RSA modulus, requiring millions of physical qubits.

buildSteps.title: Verify and repeat
buildSteps.detail: Check the factors against classical computation; refine hardware and software until results are repeatable.

prerequisites.why: no experiment has yet shown a logical qubit that beats the best physical qubit over many cycles.
machines with hundreds of physical qubits exist, but millions are needed for cryptographic factoring.
two-qubit gate errors are around 0.1–1%, still far too high for deep arithmetic circuits.
circuits for small numbers have been designed and tested, but resource estimates for large numbers remain enormous.
the classical post-processing step is well understood and runs instantly on ordinary computers.

pathway.milestone: small noisy machines factor numbers like 15 and 21
pathway.unlocks: proof that the algorithm's logic works on real hardware.

pathway.milestone: logical qubits that outperform physical qubits
pathway.unlocks: a path to scaling error-corrected machines.

pathway.milestone: small fault-tolerant processors running simple algorithms
pathway.unlocks: confidence that deep circuits can run reliably.

pathway.milestone: a quantum computer with millions of physical qubits
pathway.unlocks: breaking RSA-2048 and other public-key cryptography.
factoring even larger numbers by linking smaller processors.
